paragraphs: Unless the context otherwise requires, the terms "Company," "Patrick," "we," "our," or "us" refer to Patrick Industries, Inc. and its subsidiaries.

Patrick is a leading component solutions provider for the recreational vehicle ("RV"), marine, powersports, manufactured housing ("MH") and various industrial markets – including single and multi-family housing, hospitality, institutional and commercial markets.

The Company operates through a nationwide network that includes, as of December 31, 2025, approximately 191 manufacturing plants and 50 warehouse and distribution facilities located in 25 states, with a small presence in Mexico, China and Canada. The Company operates within two reportable segments, Manufacturing and Distribution, through a nationwide network of manufacturing and distribution centers for its products, thereby reducing in-transit delivery time and cost to the regional manufacturing footprint of its customers. The Manufacturing and Distribution segments accounted for 74% and 26%, respectively, of the Company's consolidated net sales for the year ended December, 31, 2025. Financial information about these operating segments is included in Note 17 "Segment Information" of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K (the "Form 10-K") and incorporated herein by reference.

The Company's capital allocation strategy is to optimally manage and utilize its resources and leverage its platform of operating brands to continue to grow, reinvest in its business, and return capital to shareholders. Through strategic acquisitions, expansion both geographically and into new product lines and investment in infrastructure and capital expenditures, Patrick seeks to ensure that its operating network contains capacity, technology and innovative thought processes to support anticipated growth needs, effectively respond to changes in market conditions, inventory and sales levels, and successfully integrate manufacturing, distribution and administrative functions.

Over the last three years, we have executed on a number of new product initiatives and completed acquisitions for aggregate cash consideration of approximately $560 million, net of cash acquired. These product initiatives and acquisitions directly complement our core competencies and existing products, expand our presence in our primary end markets, and position us to opportunistically enter into adjacent end markets or product categories.

Patrick believes that returning capital to shareholders is an important part of its capital allocation strategy, and during 2025 we returned $87 million to shareholders through our regular quarterly dividend and opportunistic share repurchases.

The Company was incorporated in 1959 in Indiana. The Company's principal executive and administrative offices are located at 107 West Franklin Street, Elkhart, Indiana 46516 and the telephone number is (574) 294-7511; Internet website address: www.patrickind.com. Information on our website is not incorporated in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
Patrick manufactures and distributes a variety of products within its reportable segments including:
Laminated products for furniture, shelving, walls and countertops Pre-finished wall and ceiling panels
Laminated and decorative surface products, including laminated panels, decorative and wrapped vinyls, paper-laminated panels, and vinyl printing Drywall and drywall finishing products
Solid surface, granite and quartz countertops Interior and exterior lighting products Fabricated aluminum products Wiring, electrical and plumbing products
Hardwood profile mouldings Transportation and logistics services
Electrical systems components including instrument, digital switching, dash panels, digital displays and gauges Electronics and audio systems components
Slide-out trim and fascia Cement siding Cabinet products, doors, components and custom cabinetry Raw and processed lumber

headings: Economic and business conditions beyond Patrick's control, including cyclicality and seasonality in the industries it sells products, could lead to fluctuations in and negatively impact operating results.
If the financial condition of our customers and suppliers deteriorates, our business and operating results could suffer.
Our sales are materially concentrated with two customers, the loss of either of which could have a material adverse impact on our operating results and financial condition.
Changes in consumer preferences relating to our products could adversely impact our sales levels and our operating results.
The RV, marine, powersports, MH and industrial industries are highly competitive and some of our competitors may have greater resources than we do.
Our operating results can be adversely affected by inflation, changes in the cost or availability of raw materials, energy, transportation and other necessary supplies and services.
If we cannot effectively manage the challenges and risks associated with doing business internationally, our revenues and profitability may suffer.
If we are unable to manage our inventory, our operating results could be materially and adversely affected.
Increases in demand for our products could make it more difficult for us to obtain additional skilled labor, which may adversely impact our operating efficiencies.
Fuel shortages or high prices for fuel could have an adverse impact on our operations.
Interruptions or disruptions in production at one of our key facilities could have a material adverse impact on our operations.
Our ability to integrate acquired businesses may adversely affect operations.
We may incur material charges or be adversely impacted by the consolidation and/or closure of all or part of a manufacturing or distribution facility.
The inability to attract and retain qualified executive officers and key personnel may adversely affect our operations.
We could be impacted by potential effects of union organizing activities.
We are subject to federal, state, local and certain international tax regulation. Changes thereto can have impacts on taxes paid, exposure to liabilities, and financial results of the Company.

We could experience unusual or significant litigation, governmental investigations, or adverse publicity arising out of alleged defects in products, services, perceived environmental impacts, or otherwise.
Public health emergencies, whether domestic or international, may have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial position and cash flows.
The conditional conversion feature of the 1.75% Convertible Notes due 2028 may adversely affect our financial condition and operating results.
The convertible note hedge and warrant transactions may affect the value of the 1.75% Convertible Notes and our common stock.
Risks Related to Information Security, Cybersecurity and Data Privacy
If our information technology systems fail to perform adequately, our operations could be disrupted which could adversely affect our business, reputation and results of operations.
A cyber incident or data breach could result in information theft, data corruption, operational disruption, and/or financial loss.
Certain provisions in our Articles of Incorporation and Amended and Restated By-laws may delay, defer or prevent a change in control that our shareholders might consider to be in their best interest.
Conditions within the insurance markets could impact our ability to negotiate favorable terms and conditions for various liability coverage and could potentially result in uninsured losses.
Risks Related to Ownership of our Common Stock
A variety of factors, many of which are beyond our control, could influence fluctuations in the market price for our common stock.
paragraphs: In addition to the other information set forth in this report, you should carefully consider the following factors which could materially affect our business, financial condition or results of operations. The risks described below are not the only risks we face. Additional factors not presently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial also may materially adversely affect our business, cash flows, financial condition or results of operations in future periods.

The RV, marine, powersports, MH and industrial markets in which we operate are subject to cycles of growth and contraction in consumer demand, and volatility in production levels, shipments, sales and operating results, due to external factors such as general economic conditions, consumer confidence, employment rates, financing availability, interest rates, inflation, fuel prices, and other economic conditions affecting consumer demand and discretionary spending. Periods of economic recession and downturns have adversely affected our business and operating results in the past, and have potential to adversely impact our future results. Consequently, the results for any prior period may not be indicative of results for any future period. In addition, fluctuation in demand could adversely affect our management of inventory, which could lead to an inability to meet customer needs or a charge for obsolete inventory.

Manufacturing operations in the RV, powersports, marine and MH industries historically have been seasonal and at their highest levels when the weather is moderate. Accordingly, the Company's sales and profits had generally been the highest in the second quarter and lowest in the fourth quarter. Seasonal industry trends in the past several years have included the impact related to the addition of major RV manufacturer open houses for dealers in the August-September timeframe and marine open houses in the December-February timeframe, resulting in dealers delaying certain restocking purchases until new product lines are introduced at these shows. In addition, recent seasonal industry trends have been, and future trends may be, different than in prior years due to volatile economic conditions, interest rates, access to financing, cost of fuel, national and regional economic conditions and consumer confidence on retail sales of RVs and marine units and other products for which the Company sells its components, as well as fluctuations in RV and marine dealer inventories, increased volatility in demand from RV and marine dealers, the timing of dealer orders, and from time to time, the impact of severe weather conditions on the timing of industry-wide wholesale shipments.

The markets we serve have been highly sensitive to changes in the economic environment. Weakening conditions in the economy, or the lack of available financing in the credit market, could cause the financial condition of our customers and suppliers to deteriorate, which could negatively affect our business through the loss of sales or the inability to meet our commitments. Many of our customers participate in highly competitive markets and their financial condition may deteriorate as a result. In addition, a decline in the financial condition of our customers could hinder our ability to collect amounts owed by customers.

Two customers in the RV market accounted for a combined 28% of our consolidated net sales in 2025. The loss of either of these customers could have a material adverse impact on our operating results and financial condition. We do not have long-term agreements with our customers and cannot predict that we will maintain our current relationships with these customers or that we will continue to supply them at current levels.

Changes in consumer preferences, or our inability to anticipate changes in consumer preferences for RVs, marine models, powersports products or manufactured homes, or for the products we make could reduce demand for our products and adversely affect our operating results and financial condition.

paragraphs: The Company's RV products are sold primarily to major manufacturers of RVs, smaller original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs"), and to a lesser extent, manufacturers in adjacent industries. The principal types of recreational vehicles include (1) towables: conventional travel trailers, fifth wheels, folding camping trailers, and truck campers; and (2) motorized: class A (large motor homes), class B (van campers), and class C (small-to-mid size motor homes).

The RV industry is our primary market and comprised 45% and 44% of the Company's consolidated net sales for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. Net sales to the RV industry increased 9% for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to 2024. Following a dealer inventory restocking in the first half of 2024, OEMs reduced production levels slightly in the second half of the year as dealers actively managed inventory levels as retail demand softened. In 2025, dealer inventory dynamics continued to normalize, with inventory reductions moderating as dealer inventory levels moved closer to targeted levels.

According to the RV Industry Association ("RVIA"), RV industry wholesale unit shipments totaled approximately 342,200 units in 2025, an increase of 3% compared to approximately 333,700 units in 2024. According to Company estimates based on data from Statistical Surveys, Inc. ("SSI"), RV industry retail unit sales totaled approximately 348,700 units in 2025, a decrease of 2% compared to approximately 354,400 units in 2024.

paragraphs: 除非文意另有所指，否則 "Company"、"Patrick"、"we"、"our" 或 "us" 皆指 Patrick Industries, Inc. 及其子公司。
Patrick 是遊艇（"RV"）、船用、機車、製造住宅（"MH"）及各種工業市場（包括單、多戶住宅、旅館、機構及商業市場）的主要零組件解決方案供應商。

本公司透過全國性網路運作，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，約有 191 個製造廠與 50 個倉庫及配送設施，位於 25 個州，並在墨西哥、中國及加拿大有少量據點。本公司透過全國性製造與配送中心網路，運作於製造與配送兩大應報告分部，以減少貨物在運送過程中的時間與成本，並符合客戶區域製造據點的需求。製造與配送分部分別佔本公司 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年合併淨銷售額的 74% 與 26%。有關這些營運分部的財務資訊，請參閱本年度 10-K 表報（"Form 10-K"）所附的財務會計彙編說明書附註第 17 節 "分部資訊"，並 herein 予以引用。
本公司的資本配置策略為優化管理與運用其資源，並善用其運營品牌的平台，以持續成長、重投資於業務，並回饋股東資本。透過戰略性收購、地理與產品線的擴張，以及對基礎建設與資本支出的投資，Patrick 希望確保其運營網路擁有容量、技術與創新思維，以支持預期的成長需求，有效應對市場條件、存貨與銷售水準的變化，並成功整合製造、配送與行政功能。
過去三年，我們執行了許多新的產品計畫，並完成總計約 5.6 億美元現金對價（扣除所取得現金）的收購。這些產品計畫與收購直接補強我們的核心競爭優勢與現有產品，擴大我們在主要終端市場的佔有率，並使我們有機會進入相鄰的終端市場或產品類別。
Patrick 相信回饋股東資本是其資本配置策略的重要組成部分，2025 年我們透過定期季度股息與機會性股票買回，回饋股東約 8,700 萬美元。
本公司於1959年在印第安那州設立。本公司之主要營運及行政辦公室位於107 West Franklin Street, Elkhart, Indiana 46516，電話號碼為(574) 294-7511；網際網路網站地址：www.patrickind.com。本公司網站之資訊未納入本年度10-K表式年報。
Patrick 在其應報告分部內製造與分銷多種產品，包括：
傢俱、書架、牆面及檯面用壓層產品 預處理牆面及天花板板

實質表面、花崗巖及石英檯面 內部及外部照明產品 金屬製造鋁產品 配線、電氣及水管產品

paragraphs: 本公司 RV 產品主要銷售給 RV 的主要製造商、較小的原廠設備製造商（"OEMs"）以及較少數的鄰近產業製造商。主要的休閒車類型包括（1）可拖曳型：傳統露營拖車、五分之一拖車、可摺疊露營拖車及貨車露營拖車；以及（2）動力型：A 級（大型旅居車）、B 級（貨車露營車）及 C 級（中小型旅居車）。

RV 行業為本公司主要市場，佔本公司合併後淨銷售額的 45% 及 44%，分別為 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年及 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年。2025 年 12 月 31 日財年銷售給 RV 行業的淨銷售額較 2024 年成長 9%。在 2024 年第一季經銷商庫存補貨後，原廠設備製造商在該年第二季略微減少生產量，因經銷商積極管理庫存水準，零售需求趨緩。2025 年經銷商庫存動態持續正常化，庫存減少趨緩，因經銷商庫存水準已接近目標水準。
根據 RV 行業協會（"RVIA"）的資料，2025 年 RV 行業整體銷售單位數量約為 342,200 單位，較 2024 年約 333,700 單位成長 3%。根據本公司基於 Statistical Surveys, Inc.（"SSI"）資料的估計，2025 年 RV 行業零售銷售單位數量約為 348,700 單位，較 2024 年約 354,400 單位減少 2%。

headings: 與本公司業務相關之風險
除 Patrick 控制之外的經濟與商業環境因素，包括其銷售產品之產業所面臨的週期性與季節性，可能會導致營運結果之波動並對其產生負面影響。
若本公司客戶與供應商之財務狀況惡化，將可能對本公司業務與營運結果造成影響。
本公司銷售業務高度集中於兩大客戶，若任一客戶流失，將可能對本公司營運結果與財務狀況產生重大負面影響。
消費者對本公司產品之偏好改變，可能對本公司銷售水準與營運結果產生負面影響。
RV、船艇、機車、MH 以及工業產業為高度競爭產業，部分競爭對手可能擁有較本公司更優渥之資源。
本公司營運結果可能因通貨膨脹、原材料、能源、運輸及其他必要物料與服務之成本或可得性變動而受到負面影響。
若本公司無法有效管理與國際業務相關之挑戰與風險，將可能導致營收與獲利受到影響。
若本公司無法有效管理存貨，將可能對營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司產品需求增加，可能使本公司更難取得額外的專業技術人力，這可能會對營運效率造成不利影響。
燃料短缺或燃料價格高昂可能對本公司營運造成不利影響。
本公司任一關鍵廠區之生產中斷或受擾，可能對營運造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司整合收購企業之能力可能對營運造成不利影響。
本公司可能因製造或配送廠區之合併及/或關閉，而產生重大費用或遭受不利影響。
本公司若無法吸引並留住合格之高階主管及關鍵人員，可能對營運造成不利影響。
本公司可能因工會組織活動之潛在影響而遭受不利影響。
本公司受美國聯邦、州、地方及某些國際稅務規範之制約。相關規範之變更可能影響本公司所繳納之稅款、潛在負債暴露及財務結果。
本公司可能遭遇不尋常或重大之訴訟、政府調查或因產品或服務之瑕疵、 perceived 環境影響或其他因素而產生之不利宣傳。
無論為國內或國際之公共衛生危機，均可能對本公司之業務、營運結果、財務狀況及現金流產生不利影響。
1.75% 可轉換優先債券（2028 年到期）之條件轉換特徵可能對本公司之財務狀況及營運結果產生不利影響。
可轉換債券對沖及認購權證交易可能影響 1.75% 可轉換優先債券及本公司普通股之價值。
與資訊安全、網路安全及資料隱私相關之風險
若本公司之資訊科技系統無法充分運作，可能導致營運中斷，進而對本公司之業務、聲譽及營運結果產生不利影響。
網路事件或資料外泄可能導致資訊竊取、資料毀損、營運中斷及/或財務損失。
本公司章程及修正後的規約中某些條款可能延宕、延後或防止股東認為符合其最佳利益之控制權變更。
保險市場之條件可能影響本公司與各類責任保險之投保方就有利條款與條件進行協商之能力，並可能導致未投保之損失。
持有本公司普通股之風險
多種因素，其中許多為本公司所無法控制，可能影響本公司普通股之市場價格波動。
paragraphs: 除本報告中所載之其他資訊外，您應謹慎考量下列因素，這些因素可能重大影響本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果。下列所描述之風險並非本公司所面臨之唯一風險。尚有其他未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要之因素，亦可能於未來期間重大不利影響本公司業務、現金流、財務狀況或營運成果。

本公司所從事之露營車（RV）、船艇（marine）、休閒車（powersports）、移動住宅（MH）及工業市場，會因消費者需求之成長與衰退週期，以及生產量、出貨量、銷售量及營運成果之波動，而受到外部因素影響，例如總體經濟狀況、消費者信心、就業率、融資可得性、利率、通貨膨脹、燃料價格及其他影響消費者需求與可支配支出之經濟狀況。過去經濟衰退與不景氣期間已對本公司業務及營運成果造成負面影響，未來亦可能對本公司營運成果造成負面影響。因此，任何過去期間之營運成果未必能反映未來期間之營運成果。此外，需求之波動可能對本公司存貨管理造成負面影響，導致無法滿足客戶需求或產生過時存貨之費用。

露營車（RV）、休閒車（powersports）、船艇（marine）及移動住宅（MH）產業之製造營運歷來具有季節性，且在天氣適中時達到最高點。因此，本公司之銷售與獲利通常在第二季達到最高點，第四季則為最低點。過去幾年產業之季節性趨勢包括因在八月至九月間增加大型露營車製造商為經銷商舉辦之展示會，以及在十二月至二月間舉辦之船艇展示會，導致經銷商延後某些補貨購買，直到這些展會推出新產品線為止。此外，近期產業之季節性趨勢與過去年份不同，未來趨勢亦可能不同，這是因應經濟條件波動、利率、融資可得性、燃料成本、國家與地區經濟狀況及消費者對露營車與船艇零售銷售之信心，以及本公司銷售零組件之其他產品之需求變動，以及露營車與船艇經銷商存貨之變動，增加露營車與船艇經銷商需求之波動，經銷商訂單時間，以及偶爾因極端天氣條件對產業整體批發出貨時間之影響所致。
本公司所服務之市場對經濟環境之變動極為敏感。若經濟條件惡化，或信貸市場缺乏融資可得性，可能導致客戶與供應商之財務狀況惡化，進而對本公司業務造成負面影響，例如銷售減少或無法履行本公司之承諾。許多客戶參與高度競爭之市場，其財務狀況可能因上述因素而惡化。此外，客戶財務狀況之下降可能影響本公司收取客戶應付款項之能力。
2025 年，露營車市場中兩家客戶合計佔本公司合併淨銷售額之 28%。若失去其中任一客戶，可能對本公司營運成果與財務狀況造成重大負面影響。本公司與客戶並無長期契約，無法預測本公司將維持現有與這些客戶之關係，或持續以目前水準供應這些客戶。
消費者偏好之變動，或本公司無法預測消費者對露營車、船艇、休閒車產品或製造住宅之偏好變動，或對本公司所製造產品之偏好變動，可能導致本公司產品之需求減少，進而對本公司營運成果與財務狀況造成負面影響。
